classification.difficultyReason: Read the origin maximum and labelled minimum, then classify horizontal-line heights giving one, two or three distinct intersections, including the two tangency cases.

content.prompt: The graph of $y=f(x)$ is sketched below.

spec.description: Schematic cubic-shaped curve with local maximum at the origin and labelled local minimum (4,-4), unticked axes and end arrows. Bézier construction preserves the qualitative stimulus without assigning an unprinted equation.
spec.mathematics: Turning-point heights 0 and -4; left tail down and right tail up.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied graph features remain visible in the question.

children.prompt: For what values of $k$ does the equation $f(x)=k$ have

answer.worked: A horizontal line above the local maximum or below the local minimum meets the curve once. Hence $k>0$ or $k<-4$.
At either turning-point height, a horizontal line touches the curve there and intersects another branch. Hence $k=-4$ or $k=0$.
A horizontal line strictly between the turning-point heights meets all three branches. Hence $-4<k<0$.
